SYDNEY, 2 February 2017 — Jamaica Blue believes in giving back to the community and that begins with the nation’s youth\. The company has committed to a long-term partnership with Beacon Foundation – the national charity organisation supporting young people from disadvantaged communities to complete Year 12 and successfully transition into meaningful careers\. Drew Eide, Brand Manager at Jamaica Blue, believes the partnership is a perfect fit, in that both organisations value working with young Australians to ensure they have the skills, capabilities and opportunities to be successful in life and work\. “We employ over 1,500 people in our cafés across Australia and a large number of those are under the age of 25\. We are proud of Jamaica Blue’s record of creating employment opportunities for young people and giving them an introduction to the world of work, and we see Beacon Foundation’s Programs as an extension of that,” said Drew\. Justin Dale Goldsberry, 34, of Duncan, Oklahoma, passed away on May 13, 2026, in Duncan\. Justin was born on August 7, 1991, in Duncan, Oklahoma, to Shannon Dale Jones and Caroline Goldsberry\. He spent his life in Duncan and was known for his kind and caring heart, his love of sports, and his deep love for family and friends\. Justin accepted Christ and was baptized at City Heights Baptist Church in Duncan in 2001\. He attended Empire High School and graduated with the Class of 2010\. During high school, he especially loved sports and proudly played football, basketball, and baseball, earning his letters and proudly wearing his letterman’s jacket\. Baseball was always his favorite sport, and he loved the Texas Rangers as well as the Dallas Cowboys football team\. Those who knew Justin will remember his love for his family, his caring nature, and the joy he brought to the people around him\. Justin is survived by his parents, Shannon Dale Jones and Caroline Goldsberry; his grandparents, Robert and Shernell Jones; his two sons, Jackson and Timothy; and many other family members and friends who loved him dearly\. # Busing company settles $2\.4 million lawsuit for colluding to raise prices in three Massachusetts communities, AG says - The Boston Globe An Ohio-based school bus company has agreed to pay $2\.4 million to settle a lawsuit alleging it colluded with a competitor to inflate prices in three communities, Lynn, Dedham, and Saugus, between 2022 and 2025, Attorney General Andrea Campbell said Monday\. Beacon Mobility Corporation, which mainly provides special education busing service through** **a pair of subsidiaries, agreed to settle accusations that it worked with an unnamed competitor to fix busing rates and undermine the competitive bidding process, Campbell said\. According to the settlement, Beacon inflated contract prices by agreeing not to compete with the other company over certain district contracts in exchange for it doing the same in communities where Beacon held the contract\. “When companies engage in unlawful collusion that increase costs for municipalities, it reduces their ability to fund other critical programs including our libraries, public safety agencies and schools,” Campbell said in a statement\.
